title: Tide Original Liquid vs Kirkland Signature Ultra Clean Liquid

brand.product: Tide Original Liquid Laundry Detergent, 132 fl oz (100 loads)

alternative.product: Kirkland Signature Ultra Clean HE Liquid Laundry Detergent, 194 fl oz (146 loads)

summary: Consumer Reports names Kirkland Ultra Clean its best-value liquid detergent, placing just behind Tide in its tests at roughly half the cost per load.
evidence: Consumer Reports' liquid detergent tests (reported 2022 and again in Aug 2026) rank Kirkland Signature Ultra Clean in the top five of 49 liquids, directly behind four Tide products. It matched Tide on body oil and salad dressing stains and in hard water. Tide prices were taken from Walmart; the Kirkland price is Costco's online price as reported in an April 2026 deal post.
differences: Not identical formulas. Tide scored better on tough stains such as grass and blood, so Tide still wins if those are your main problem. Kirkland is sold mainly at Costco (membership needed; third-party Walmart sellers charge about $32).

aspects.brand: Tide products rank just above Kirkland in CR's liquid tests
aspects.alternative: Top five liquid, behind four Tide products; matched Tide in hard water

aspects.brand: Better on grass and blood stains
aspects.alternative: Not quite as good as Tide on grass and blood

aspects.aspect: Body oil and salad dressing stains
aspects.alternative: Kept up with Tide's top offerings

aspects.aspect: Cost per load (per CR via Hunker)

title: Cascade Platinum ActionPacs vs Kirkland Signature UltraShine Pacs

brand.product: Cascade Platinum ActionPacs Dishwasher Detergent, Lemon, 62 count

key_ingredients.name: Enzyme dishwasher detergent pac (full formula proprietary)

alternative.product: Kirkland Signature Platinum Performance UltraShine Dishwasher Detergent Pacs, 115 count

key_ingredients.name: Enzyme dishwasher detergent pac (full formula proprietary)

summary: Consumer Reports rates Kirkland UltraShine pacs Excellent at cleaning and film resistance, the same top tier as Cascade, for about a third of the price per load.
evidence: Consumer Reports' dishwasher detergent tests rated Kirkland Signature Platinum Performance UltraShine Excellent on food removal and film resistance and named it a Best Buy; Cascade ActionPacs were also rated Excellent and recommended. CR's model page confirms the 115-count pac with enzymes. Kirkland price is the typical Costco warehouse price from a price tracker (range $11.59-$12.99); CR lists it online from $20.99 delivered.
differences: Different proprietary formulas; CR tested Cascade ActionPacs and Platinum lines, not a direct like-for-like lab comparison of this exact Cascade SKU. Kirkland needs a Costco membership; the online price is higher than in-warehouse.

aspects.brand: Cascade ActionPacs with Dawn: Excellent cleaning test, Recommended (CR, Apr 2022)
aspects.alternative: Excellent on food removal and film resistance, CR Best Buy, 9 cents per dose (CR, Apr 2022)

title: Clorox Disinfecting Bleach vs up&up Regular Bleach

brand.product: Clorox Disinfecting Bleach, Regular, 121 fl oz

alternative.product: up&up Regular Bleach with Fabric Protection, 121 fl oz

summary: Both are 7.5% sodium hypochlorite regular bleach in the same 121 oz size, so they bleach and disinfect the same way when diluted per label.
evidence: Target's product pages list sodium hypochlorite at 7.5% for both Clorox Disinfecting Bleach (Regular) and up&up Regular Bleach with Fabric Protection. Both are sold in 121 fl oz jugs at Target.
differences: Savings are modest (about 12%). Neither Target page shows the EPA registration number, so check the up&up jug for an EPA Reg. No. before relying on it for disinfection claims. The up&up product adds a fabric-protection claim; the additives are not disclosed. The up&up page shows no EPA registration number, so its disinfecting claim isn't verified.

aspects.brand: EPA Reg. No. 5813-120; label says kills 99.9% of viruses and bacteria when used as directed
aspects.alternative: Target page makes no disinfecting claim and shows no EPA Reg. No. (only "EPA" in the URL); staff answer: cannot be relied on to kill C. diff
Added fabric-protection additive, undisclosed; not colour-safe

title: OxiClean Versatile vs up&up Powder Stain Remover

brand.product: OxiClean Versatile Stain Remover Powder, 3 lb (48 oz)

alternative.product: up&up Powder Stain Remover, Unscented, 56 oz

summary: Both are sodium carbonate plus sodium percarbonate oxygen-bleach powders with a nonionic ethoxylate surfactant, listed in the same order.
evidence: Church & Dwight's ingredient disclosure for OxiClean Versatile lists sodium carbonate, sodium carbonate peroxide (sodium percarbonate), C10-16 alketh surfactant, fragrance, sodium chloride and colorant. Target lists up&up Powder Stain Remover as sodium carbonate, sodium percarbonate, laureth-7, sodium silicate and colorant. Same active oxygen-bleach chemistry in the same order, but neither discloses percentages.
differences: Percentages are not disclosed, so active oxygen content may differ. up&up is unscented and uses sodium silicate instead of sodium chloride; OxiClean contains fragrance. Savings are modest (about 15% per oz); Target sometimes prices it lower (Shipt showed $6.79).

aspects.brand: Sodium carbonate, sodium carbonate peroxide, C10-16 alcohol ethoxylate, fragrance, sodium chloride, blue pigment
aspects.alternative: Sodium carbonate, sodium percarbonate, laureth-7, sodium silicate, colorant
Listed as 'Unscented', but shoppers dispute it; some reviewers report a scent

title: Mr. Clean Magic Eraser Extra Durable vs Amazon Basics Extra Durable Cleaning Eraser

brand.product: Mr. Clean Magic Eraser Extra Durable, 10 count

alternative.product: Amazon Basics Extra Durable Cleaning Erasers, 14 count

summary: A Magic Eraser is a block of melamine foam, and Amazon's cleaning erasers are the same kind of melamine foam pad for less per pad.
evidence: P&G Professional distributor listings describe the Magic Eraser as a melamine foam pad, and Apartment Therapy explains it works because melamine foam acts like very fine sandpaper. Amazon Basics Extra Durable Cleaning Erasers are the same product type, and buyers report similar results on tubs and scuffs. Prices are the usual non-sale Amazon prices shown on deal listings.
differences: Reviewers say the Amazon pads are slightly thinner, so each may wear out sooner, and density is not published for either. Mr. Clean's version is branded Durafoam. Both are frequently discounted with coupons and Subscribe & Save.

aspects.brand: Mr. Clean Magic Eraser melamine pad
aspects.alternative: Buyer on a deal post: 'similar to the Mr Clean brand', similar on tub and door scuffs
Same buyer: Amazon pads are slimmer, about the same width
